decision.title: XSLT conformance sweep after the Phase 4 gate (packet 4.19)

body.p: , after , , , , , . Verified as asks: the debug preset, the unit and CLI tests touched, clang-tidy and the call-cycle check on the files changed, and the whole XT40 suite with the release driver after each change, compared case by case (it runs in about a minute here). XT40 8,650 to 8,759 passed, 0 errors, no case lost.

item.p: Type patterns "~T" (priority, 34 failing): not implemented, by . The project's draft (13 October 2026) has no type patterns: PR 2911 (14 September 2026) replaced them with atomic(), record(), map and array patterns, which sxml has; "~T" survives only in a few examples and in the typed attribute of xsl:mode. The suite's priority cases are written against the older draft, and its other expectations there (priority 1.0 for ".[p]", 0.25 for "{42}" and "array({'x'})") contradict 6.4 of the project's draft too. Nothing in priority changes.

Extension instructions call named templates (10.1.3; call-template -ext 7 to 32 of 32): an extension instruction named after a template it binds to is xsl:call-template of it; each attribute is parsed while lowering, as a kept AST (, sxml_xslt_lowering_parse_attribute), as a value template for an xs:boolean or atomic parameter (boolean words; xs:untypedAtomic) or as an expression otherwise.

xsl:item-type and xsl:record-type (5.4, ; record 22 to 39, type-alias 13 to 25): src/xslt_named_type.c does what XQuery's declare type and declare record do: the static context's named item types (resolved in rounds; XPST0051, XTSE4035, XTSE4030) and nominative records in the type registry (XTSE4050). Both are components of a new package component kind, item type, so packages bind them by 3.4.5.5. xsl:field takes the draft's static and select. Delayed (): the record constructor function (5.4.2.2).

Available documents are source documents (4.2.2; snapshot 16 to 34, and merge, document): a transformation strips each available document once and hands the copies to fn:doc; a global context item that is one becomes its copy. fn:snapshot of a namespace node.

merge (67 to 79; 29 more need streaming): the XSLT driver serves collections (also collection 0 to 5); XTSE1060, XTSE1070, XTSE3470, XTSE3500 for the current-group functions in patterns; XTDE2210 for fixed merge-key attributes that differ (raised when evaluated); XTTE2230 for incomparable merge keys. Left: XTDE3490 (map:get of an unknown source name, in src/xpath_lower.c), XTDE2220, computed XTDE2210, validation codes.

Errors in included modules ('s accepted design, done): each static context's IR module has its stylesheet module's URI as source name, and templates, stylesheet functions, attribute sets and global initializers take their element's IR module. Inline functions and xsl:iterate bodies keep module 0.

Duplicates ('s list): sxml_allocator_allocate_array (src/memory_internal.h) is the one array allocation helper; the XSLT copies use it, the others move when their files are next touched. The key equality of group-adjacent and group-starting-with stays: the FLWOR's keys_are_equal is in src/xquery_flwor.c, another packet's file at the time.

match="$var" membership: not done ('s accepted design stays open). The parts exist: the evaluation memo () that keeps key indexes and cached calls, and a map from generate-id() to the node, built once by the cached-call row for a pattern rooted at a global variable, makes each test one lookup. The match expression is an XPath AST, so it needs a private function name it can call, or the match lowering must bind the index as a pattern variable; the rows live in src/function_library_xslt.c, another packet's file at the time.
